title: Moss and Mipsy's Floating Fun
markdown:
Moss the little ogre lived in the green rolling hills where gentle winds whispered sleepy songs through tall soft pines. His heart was as warm as the moss that tickled his cheeks. His most favorite thing in the whole wide world was Mipsy, a baby goat, a tiny ball of fluffy white wool whose little hooves went tip-tap-tip-tap, usually right behind him.

One sunny morning the air smelled of clover and warm earth. “Mipsy, my darling little fluffball,” Moss whispered, voice like rustling leaves, “it is time for a little adventure.” He imagined juicy red berries, or a smooth grey stone from the stream. “We will go into the pine wood, and you shall find a pretty thing.”

Mipsy baa-baa’d and wiggled her tail. Tip-tap-tip-tap into the wood they went. Trees stood like kind giants. Golden sunbeams danced on leafy ground. Peaceful. Quiet. Lovely.

Moss found a smooth grey stone. “Watch me. I will toss this, and you will bring it back.” The stone rolled into pine needles. Mipsy watched. Then: flutter flutter flutter. A butterfly with wings like painted sunset clouds. She forgot the stone and went tip-tap-tip-tap after it, goat-heart happy.

Moss chuckled, rumbling. “Not the butterfly, my sweet girl, the stone!” He waved it. Just then a shimmering cloak like twilight floated by, a kind smile, a silvery umbrella twinkling with starlight. Witch Willow, wise eyes like friendly stars.

“Hello, dear Moss. Hello, little Mipsy. A lovely day for a walk.”

Moss sighed a soft puff. “I am trying to teach Mipsy a trick, but she likes butterflies more than fetching.”

Willow’s smile warmed the clearing. “Perhaps the trick is not quite Mipsy’s favourite. What does she love most?”

Mipsy had forgotten the butterfly and was batting a fluffy dandelion with her nose. Boop. Seeds flew like little white fairies. “She loves… things that float.”

Tip-tap-tip-tap. Things that float.

“Exactly.” Willow plucked a dandelion. “Blow, very gently, like a sleepy sigh.” Moss whooshed. Seeds swirled, tiny white clouds.

Mipsy’s eyes widened. She baa-baa’d with joy and tried to catch one on her nose. Boop. Another seed floated. She wiggled. Moss laughed, warm.

“This is the most wonderful trick. Teaching Mipsy to make things float.”

Willow twinkled. The sun dipped, soft colours. Moss felt a lovely tiredness and scooped Mipsy into mossy arms. “Time to go home. Dream of floating seeds.”

She yawned, contented, against his chest. First faint stars like tiny diamonds. He hummed a sleepy tune. Welcoming lights glowed ahead, blankets and peaceful dreams. Tip-tap-tip-tap had become a float, and everything, with a heart full of goat, was just right.
audience: children aged 3-4, story time at home
author: StoryGen Community
